root_cause: The RISC-V Build (RVV 1.0) job failed during 'CMake - Configure' in approximately 37 seconds. This is far shorter than expected for a full RISC-V cross-compilation configure (which normally takes several minutes). Job logs are inaccessible (GitHub API 403 Forbidden), preventing direct inspection. The triggered PR (#36955) only modifies Windows-specific TBB DLL copy logic in src/cmake/openvino.cmake (inside `if(WIN32 AND BUILD_SHARED_LIBS)` guard), which is irrelevant to RISC-V builds that use THREADING=OMP and run on Linux. The same PR had a transient ARM64 runner failure earlier (run 30351149892, investigation 2026-07-28-11-15-51) which succeeded on attempt 2. The combination of abnormally short configure time, inaccessible logs, and same-PR ARM64 transient failure strongly suggests a transient runner/infrastructure issue rather than a code defect. The PR change cannot be the root cause of a cmake configure failure on RISC-V/Linux/OMP.
reproduction_steps: N/A - logs are inaccessible and the failure is suspected to be transient infrastructure
recommended_actions: Re-add PR #36955 to the merge queue - the cmake change does not affect RISC-V builds
Monitor RISC-V runner pool health around 2026-07-28T12:00Z
If failure recurs, escalate to GitHub Support to investigate runner availability
prevention_strategies: Consider adding retry logic for cmake configure steps in cross-compilation builds. Ensure RISC-V runner pool has sufficient capacity and health monitoring.
